en: This is the Moon's near side, the face we see from the Earth.
This is the Moon's near side, the face we see from the Earth
Its dark patches are called seas, but there is no water.
Its dark patches are called seas, but there is no water
They are flat ground, covered by hardened lava.

They are flat ground,
covered by hardened lava
But turn the Moon to its far side, and there are hardly any seas.
But turn the Moon to its far side, and there are hardly any seas
It is pitted all over, crater upon crater.
It is pitted all over, crater upon crater
Did the Earth shield the near side?

Did the Earth
shield the near side?
No. Rocks fell on the near side and the far side about alike.
No. Rocks fell on the near and far sides about alike
At first, the near side was pitted too.

At first,
the near side
was pitted too

Why did it rise
only on the near side?
Cut the Moon in half, and its crust is thin on the near side, and thick on the far side.
Cut the Moon in half: its crust is thin on the near side, thick on the far side
The molten rock broke through only where it was thin.

The molten rock
broke through
only where it was thin

the crust differ?

heat-making elements gathered under it,

a great impact stirred the inside,
